scenes.headline: How Cloudflare OS lets agents work before you approve
scenes.sub: Gatekeepers, simulated writes and a batch approval queue
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Kheer! Here is how Cloudflare's agent workspace lets an agent finish before you approve a single write.

scenes.text: Every outside call goes through a gatekeeper: reads run and are logged, writes are queued and simulated, so the agent keeps working.
scenes.say: Every outside call goes through a gatekeeper. Reads run and get logged. Writes are queued and simulated, so the agent keeps working.

steps.say: The agent's code runs in an isolate with no network. Its only way out is a binding to a gatekeeper.
A read goes to the service, and is recorded in the action log before the data comes back.
A write is not sent. It is logged as pending, and the gatekeeper answers as if it happened.
Later you approve the batch, and only then are the writes applied for real.

left.title: Approve every step
items: Agent stops at the first write
You come back to no progress
left.say: The usual loop stops the agent at its first write, so people switch approvals off.

right.title: Approve the batch later
right.say: Here the writes are simulated, the agent finishes, and you review it all in one pass.

steps.say: On the read side: authorize the resource, call the service, record an observation.
On the action side: simulate the result, queue it, and apply once approved.

scenes.title: Skipping the human needs all three
scenes.say: A write can skip the queue only when three things line up.

items.say: The gatekeeper's author marks that action as safe to auto approve.
You switch on a rule for that kind of action.
And the workspace has never read restricted data. Once it has, nothing auto approves again.

scenes.label: gatekeeper Workers ship in the repo
scenes.note: some cannot simulate, so the agent waits
scenes.say: Sixteen gatekeepers ship in the repo. Some cannot simulate, so the agent's turn pauses until you decide.

scenes.text: Simulation is what makes approval asynchronous, and you only get it where the gatekeeper can model the service.
scenes.mark: Simulation is what makes approval asynchronous
scenes.say: Simulation is what makes approval asynchronous. You only get it where the gatekeeper can model the service.
Reads run and are logged. Writes queue up and are simulated. You approve the batch later.
